title: Verapamil in WWOX-LoF
summary: A test of barrier transport versus systemic exposure and calcium currents.

graph.evidence: Cortical co-drug exposure rose after local verapamil in kindled rats.
graph.inference: The published curves lack free blood data by treatment arm.
graph.hypothesis: Activity may induce a drug-delivery deficit in some WWOX barriers.
graph.experiment: Match free systemic co-drug and measure native neural exposure and function.

evidence: Reconstructed cortical extracellular exposure increased about 25% for phenytoin and 15% for carbamazepine in a local rat comparison. The pediatric placebo-controlled study detected no significant between-arm difference.
inference: Verapamil PET tracer experiments measure transport of the tracer and inhibition by a different compound. Circulating co-drug, norverapamil, and direct calcium-current effects remain relevant alternatives.
hypothesis: A functional ABCB1 bottleneck could restrict an independently verified co-drug after sustained activity. Baseline WWOX bulk RNA and marker-scaled contrasts do not measure luminal transport.
experiment: Measure unbound co-drug on both sides of the barrier and verify ABCB1 engagement. At fixed neural co-drug, read residual current and recurrence.
limits: Retain as a laboratory comparator. Juvenile exposure, WWOX transport and cardiovascular tolerability limit pediatric priority.
